subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What inbound-media isolation boundary should OpenClaw enforce across accounts, agents, sessions, tenants, and explicit media sharing?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but the fix sets a durable security and compatibility contract across core media storage, plugin/channel callers, managed URIs, sandbox staging, and existing flat files.

options.title: Define scoped contract first
options.body: Choose the canonical scope, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

options.title: Implement account scoping
options.body: Use channel account IDs as the first isolation key and accept follow-up work for non-1:1 account-to-agent, tenant, and sharing cases.

options.title: Split into narrower channel work
options.body: Defer the broad core contract and let channel-specific issues such as Feishu or channel provenance proceed independently.

recommendation.title: Define scoped contract first
recommendation.body: Choose the canonical scope, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent related media/staging history and already reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
